Privacy Policy

Last updated: July 7, 2026

This Privacy Policy explains how iD! Training & Development collects, uses, stores, protects, and shares personal data when you visit our website or use our portal, accounts, forms, digital products, downloads, training services, courses, examinations, assessments, and related services (together, the "Services").

1. Who is responsible for your personal data

The controller responsible for the processing described in this Privacy Policy is:

iD! Training & Development
Vennootschap onder firma (VOF)
Chamber of Commerce number: 61841277
VAT identification number: NL854512044B01
Rusthoven 26
5655 CN Eindhoven
North Brabant
The Netherlands
Email: compliance@id-develops.com

You can use the email address above for questions about this Privacy Policy or to exercise your privacy rights.

2. When an organisation provides access

An employer, school, training provider, customer, or other organisation may arrange access to the Services for its employees, contractors, students, trainees, or other authorised users.

In those situations, the organisation may determine why certain personal data is processed, such as enrolment information, participation records, progress, examination attempts, and results. The organisation may therefore be an independent controller for some processing activities.

We may process such information on the organisation's instructions or for our own legitimate purposes, such as operating and securing the platform, maintaining required records, and complying with legal obligations. Questions about an organisation's own use of your information should also be directed to that organisation.

3. Personal data we collect

The personal data we collect depends on how you interact with the Services.

3.1 Account and identity information

  • Name and email address.
  • Username or account identifier.
  • Password hash and authentication information.
  • Account role, permissions, status, and organisation.
  • Language and communication preferences.
  • Account creation, confirmation, login, and security timestamps.

We do not store your password in readable form. Passwords are processed using password-hashing mechanisms.

3.2 Contact, registration, and form information

  • Name, email address, telephone number, and organisation details.
  • Questions, messages, preferences, and information submitted through forms.
  • Course, product, or service selections.
  • Information needed to respond to an enquiry or provide a requested service.

3.3 Training and assessment information

  • Course registrations, participation, and progress.
  • Examination and assessment attempts.
  • Answers, uploaded files, scores, feedback, and results.
  • Start times, completion times, deadlines, and attempt status.
  • Records relating to suspected technical problems or assessment irregularities.
  • Certificates or completion records where applicable.

3.4 Order, billing, and payment information

  • Products and services ordered.
  • Billing name, billing address, and applicable tax information.
  • Order status, payment status, currency, amount, and transaction reference.
  • Invoice and accounting records.
  • Limited payment-method information supplied by the payment provider, such as the payment type or last digits of a card where available.

Payments may be processed by Stripe or another payment provider. Complete payment-card details are generally submitted directly to the payment provider and are not stored by us.

3.5 Uploaded content and communications

  • Files, images, audio, documents, and other materials you upload.
  • Support requests and correspondence with us.
  • Feedback, complaints, and other communications.
  • Administrative notes reasonably required to provide or support the Services.

Please do not submit sensitive or confidential personal data unless it is necessary for the requested Service and you are authorised to provide it.

3.6 Technical and usage information

  • IP address.
  • Browser type, operating system, and device information.
  • Requested pages, request times, response status, and referring page.
  • Login, authentication, fraud-prevention, and security logs.
  • Cookie identifiers and consent preferences.
  • Language, session, and portal preferences.
  • Error reports and information needed to diagnose technical problems.

We do not attempt to collect your precise device location unless a specific feature expressly requires it and an appropriate legal basis exists.

3.7 Information received from organisations

If an organisation registers you for a Service, we may receive information such as your name, email address, organisation, department, assigned course, access permissions, employee or student identifier, and other information required to administer the arrangement.

4. How and why we use personal data

We use personal data for the purposes and legal bases described below.

4.1 Providing the Services

We process account, registration, order, training, assessment, and communication information to:

  • Create and administer accounts.
  • Provide portal and product access.
  • Deliver courses, downloads, training, and other purchased or requested Services.
  • Administer examinations and assessments.
  • Calculate, record, and display results.
  • Provide feedback, support, and service communications.
  • Manage cancellations, refunds, and access periods.

The legal basis is normally performance of a contract or taking steps at your request before entering into a contract. Where access is arranged by an organisation, the legal basis may also be our legitimate interest and the organisation's legitimate interest in administering the agreed training or assessment service.

4.2 Processing orders and payments

We process order, billing, transaction, and account information to accept payments, issue invoices, confirm purchases, prevent duplicate or fraudulent transactions, and maintain financial records.

The legal bases are performance of a contract, compliance with legal and tax obligations, and our legitimate interest in preventing fraud and maintaining accurate business records.

4.3 Communications and customer support

We use contact, account, order, and technical information to answer questions, resolve technical problems, process requests, send confirmations, and provide important notices about accounts, purchases, assessments, security, or changes to the Services.

The legal bases are performance of a contract and our legitimate interest in supporting users and operating the Services effectively.

4.4 Platform security and abuse prevention

We process technical, account, security, and usage information to:

  • Authenticate users and protect accounts.
  • Detect unauthorised access, attacks, malware, spam, fraud, and other misuse.
  • Enforce access restrictions and examination rules.
  • Investigate security incidents and technical failures.
  • Maintain logs, backups, availability, and system integrity.

The legal basis is our legitimate interest in protecting users, personal data, our business, and the security and reliability of the Services. Processing may also be necessary to comply with legal obligations.

4.5 Assessment administration and integrity

We process assessment responses, attempts, timing information, technical records, and results to administer assessments, calculate scores, investigate irregularities, correct errors, and protect the integrity of the assessment process.

The legal bases are performance of a contract and our legitimate interests, and those of the organisation arranging the assessment, in providing accurate and reliable assessments.

4.6 Improving the Services

We may use usage information, error reports, feedback, and aggregated or anonymised information to understand how the Services are used, fix problems, improve workflows, and develop training and assessment content.

The legal basis is our legitimate interest in improving the quality, security, and usability of the Services. Where reasonably possible, we use aggregated or anonymised information for this purpose.

We do not use identifiable private examination answers or uploaded customer files to train general artificial-intelligence models unless we have separately informed you and established an appropriate legal basis.

4.7 Legal, accounting, and dispute purposes

We process information where necessary to comply with tax, accounting, consumer, data-protection, regulatory, and other legal obligations. We may also retain and use information to establish, exercise, or defend legal claims.

The legal bases are compliance with legal obligations and our legitimate interest in protecting our legal position.

4.8 Marketing

We may send marketing communications where you have consented or where another lawful basis permits us to do so. You can unsubscribe at any time by using the unsubscribe option in the message or by contacting us.

Withdrawing from marketing does not prevent us from sending necessary account, purchase, assessment, security, or service communications.

5. Automated scoring and decisions

Some examinations, quizzes, and assessments may be scored automatically based on predefined answer rules. Automated scoring may produce a result, progress status, or recommendation.

Unless we clearly state otherwise, these results are intended for educational, placement, coaching, or internal training purposes and are not used by us to make decisions that produce legal effects or similarly significant effects concerning you.

Results may be reviewed, corrected, or invalidated where there is evidence of a technical problem, configuration error, incorrect answer key, or assessment irregularity. You may contact us if you believe an automatically calculated result is incorrect.

Where an organisation uses a result to make its own employment, education, or other decision, that organisation is responsible for its decision-making and for providing any additional privacy information required by law.

6. When we share personal data

We do not sell personal data.

We may share personal data only where reasonably necessary with the following recipients:

6.1 Service providers

We use service providers that support the operation of the Services, which may include:

  • Cloud and application-hosting providers.
  • Database and backup providers.
  • Content-delivery, security, and network providers.
  • Object-storage providers, including Cloudflare R2.
  • Payment providers, including Stripe.
  • Email-delivery and communication providers.
  • Error-monitoring, logging, and technical-support providers.
  • Analytics providers, but only where such analytics are enabled.
  • Professional advisers such as accountants, legal advisers, and auditors.

Providers that process personal data on our behalf are required to process it only for the relevant services and to apply appropriate contractual, confidentiality, and security protections.

6.2 Organisations arranging access

If an organisation arranged or paid for your access, we may share information with authorised representatives of that organisation where this is part of the agreed service and has been disclosed to you.

Depending on the arrangement, this may include your account status, participation, progress, examination attempts, completion information, scores, results, and relevant support or integrity information.

6.3 Legal and safety disclosures

We may disclose information where reasonably necessary to comply with a legal obligation, court order, lawful authority request, or to establish, exercise, or defend legal claims. We may also share information where necessary to protect the security, rights, or safety of users, another person, or the Services.

6.4 Business changes

If our business is reorganised, transferred, merged, or sold, relevant personal data may be disclosed to professional advisers and transferred to the successor organisation, subject to applicable data-protection requirements.

7. International transfers

We are established in the Netherlands, but some service providers may process personal data in or provide access from countries outside the European Economic Area.

Where personal data is transferred outside the European Economic Area, we use an appropriate legal mechanism where required. Depending on the provider and destination, this may include:

  • An adequacy decision adopted by the European Commission.
  • The European Commission's Standard Contractual Clauses.
  • The EU-US Data Privacy Framework where applicable.
  • Additional technical, organisational, and contractual safeguards.

Information about the safeguards used for a particular transfer can be requested by contacting us. Certain details may be redacted where required to protect security or confidential commercial information.

8. How long we retain personal data

We retain personal data only for as long as reasonably necessary for the relevant purpose, including providing the Services, maintaining security, meeting contractual commitments, complying with legal obligations, and resolving disputes.

Our general retention periods are:

  • Account information: while the account remains active and normally for up to two years after the account is closed or becomes inactive, unless a longer period is needed for an active agreement, dispute, organisational record, or legal obligation.
  • Training, progress, and assessment records: for the applicable access period and normally for up to five years after completion or the last relevant activity, unless a different period is agreed with the customer or required for certification, disputes, or legal obligations.
  • Incomplete or abandoned examination attempts: normally for up to two years after the attempt, unless required as part of an active training record, integrity investigation, or organisational agreement.
  • Orders, invoices, transactions, and accounting records: generally for at least seven years where required under Dutch tax or accounting rules.
  • Contact enquiries and support correspondence: normally for up to two years after the enquiry is resolved, unless the communication forms part of a contract, complaint, dispute, or legally required record.
  • Security and technical logs: normally for up to 12 months, unless a longer period is reasonably necessary to investigate an incident, prevent abuse, or establish or defend a legal claim.
  • Uploaded files: for as long as the associated account, product, examination, administrative workflow, or agreement requires them, followed by deletion within a reasonable operational period.
  • Marketing records: until consent is withdrawn or you object, after which we may retain minimal suppression information to ensure that we respect your preference.
  • Cookie and consent records: for the periods described in our Cookie Policy or for as long as reasonably necessary to demonstrate and respect your choices.

We may retain information for longer where required by law, where a claim or investigation is ongoing, or where deletion would interfere with the rights of another person. When data is no longer required, it is deleted, anonymised, or securely isolated until deletion is technically completed.

9. Cookies and similar technologies

We use necessary cookies and similar technologies for functions such as authentication, session security, anti-forgery protection, language preferences, cookie choices, checkout, and portal operation.

We may also use analytics, marketing, or embedded third-party technologies where they are enabled and where any legally required consent has been obtained.

More information about the technologies used, their purposes, providers, and duration is available in our Cookie Policy.

10. Security

We use appropriate technical and organisational measures designed to protect personal data against accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorised disclosure, and unauthorised access.

Depending on the relevant system, these measures may include:

  • HTTPS encryption for data transmitted through the website.
  • Password hashing and authenticated account access.
  • Role-based access controls.
  • Restricted administrative access.
  • Private storage and time-limited signed upload or access URLs where applicable.
  • Security logging, monitoring, backups, and software updates.
  • Access restrictions for infrastructure, databases, and production systems.
  • Contractual and security requirements for relevant service providers.

No system can be guaranteed to be completely secure. You are responsible for keeping your login details confidential and for contacting us promptly if you suspect unauthorised access to your account.

11. Your privacy rights

Subject to the conditions and exceptions under applicable law, you may have the right to:

  • Access: request confirmation of whether we process your personal data and receive a copy of relevant data.
  • Rectification: ask us to correct inaccurate or incomplete personal data.
  • Erasure: ask us to delete personal data where there is no valid reason to continue processing it.
  • Restriction: ask us to limit processing in certain circumstances.
  • Data portability: receive certain data in a structured, commonly used, and machine-readable format and, where technically feasible, have it transmitted to another controller.
  • Object: object to processing based on legitimate interests, including relevant profiling, based on your particular situation.
  • Object to direct marketing: object at any time to the use of your personal data for direct marketing.
  • Withdraw consent: withdraw consent at any time where processing relies on consent.
  • Automated decisions: obtain information about, and where applicable challenge, certain decisions based solely on automated processing that produce legal or similarly significant effects.

Withdrawing consent does not affect the lawfulness of processing performed before the withdrawal. Some information may need to be retained despite a request where this is required by law, necessary to perform an agreement, protect another person's rights, maintain assessment integrity, or establish, exercise, or defend legal claims.

12. How to exercise your rights

To exercise a privacy right, email compliance@id-develops.com.

Please describe your request clearly and identify the account, order, organisation, or Service to which it relates. We may request information needed to verify your identity and prevent unauthorised disclosure.

We will respond within the period required by applicable law. Under the GDPR, this is normally within one month. That period may be extended where legally permitted due to the complexity or number of requests, in which case we will inform you.

Privacy requests are normally handled without charge. A reasonable fee may be charged, or a request may be refused, where permitted by law because it is manifestly unfounded or excessive.

13. Complaints

We encourage you to contact us first so that we can investigate and try to resolve your concern. You also have the right to submit a complaint to the supervisory authority in the country where you live or work, or where you believe an infringement occurred.

In the Netherlands, the supervisory authority is:

Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens
Dutch Data Protection Authority

Information about submitting a complaint is available through the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens website.

14. Children and young users

Some training or assessment Services may be used by children or young people where access is arranged by a parent, legal guardian, school, employer, training provider, or another authorised organisation.

We do not knowingly ask a child to independently provide consent for processing where parental or guardian authorisation is legally required. Where consent is used as the legal basis for an online service offered directly to a child, we will take reasonable steps to obtain or verify the required authorisation.

Parents, guardians, and organisations arranging access must provide only the information reasonably necessary for the Service and must ensure that they are authorised to do so.

If you believe that a child's personal data has been provided or processed without appropriate authorisation, contact us at compliance@id-develops.com.

15. External websites and embedded content

The Services may contain links to independent external websites or embedded third-party content. Those third parties may process personal data under their own privacy policies. We recommend reviewing their privacy information before interacting with an external service.

This Privacy Policy does not govern processing independently determined by third parties that we do not control.

16. Changes to this Privacy Policy

We may update this Privacy Policy to reflect changes to our Services, providers, security measures, legal obligations, or processing activities.

The current version will be published on this page and identified by the "Last updated" date. Where a change materially affects how we process personal data, we will take reasonable steps to provide additional notice where required.

17. Contact

For questions, privacy requests, or complaints relating to this Privacy Policy, contact:
